items.readable_text:
Content:
How can we subtract fractions, like [MATH: \dfrac{2}{4} - \dfrac{5}{4}?]

Content:
Since both fractions have the same denominator ([MATH: 4]), we can combine them into one fraction.

Content:
[MATH: (2)/(4) − (5)/(4)|= (2 − 5)/(4)]

Content:
Now, we work out [MATH: 2-5] using our number line:

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/925a065990a1c69442392d302af005da]

Content:
We get [MATH: 2-5=-3,] and therefore

Content:
[MATH: (2 − 5)/(4) = (− 3)/(4) = − (3)/(4).]

Content:
Note: If two fractions have different denominators, we need to put them over a common denominator first and then subtract!

Since both fractions have the same denominators, we can combine them into one fraction, which gives [MATH: \dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{11}{12} = \dfrac{5 - 11}{12}.]

Now, we work out [MATH: 5 - 11] using a number line:

So, we get [MATH: \dfrac{5 - 11}{12} = \dfrac{-6}{12} = -\dfrac{6}{12}.]

Finally, we simplify: [MATH: -\dfrac{6}{12} = -\dfrac{6 \div 6}{12 \div 6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}]

Therefore, we conclude that [MATH: \dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{11}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{2}.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we write [MATH: 2 \, \dfrac{2}{3}] as an improper fraction: [MATH: 2 \,\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{(2 \times 3) + 2}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}]

Since both fractions have the same denominators, we can combine them into one fraction, which gives [MATH: \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{1 - 8}{3}.]

Now, we work out [MATH: 1 - 8] using a number line:

So, we get [MATH: \dfrac{1 - 8}{3} = \dfrac{-7}{3} = -\dfrac{7}{3}.]

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

[MATH: -\dfrac{7}{3} = -2 \, \dfrac{1}{3}]

Item 2 — Example: Subtracting a Positive Fraction From a Fraction

Example Prompt:
Find the value of [MATH: \dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{11}{12}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
Since both fractions have the same denominators, we can combine them into one fraction, which gives
[MATH: \dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{11}{12} = \dfrac{5 - 11}{12}.]

Now, we work out [MATH: 5 - 11] using a number line:

[IMG: /graphics/7d88b4807862164068541f2bb1cc7df8]

So, we get
[MATH: \dfrac{5 - 11}{12} = \dfrac{-6}{12} = -\dfrac{6}{12}.]

Finally, we simplify:
[MATH: -\dfrac{6}{12} = -\dfrac{6 \div 6}{12 \div 6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}]

Therefore, we conclude that
[MATH: \dfrac{5}{12} - \dfrac{11}{12} = -\dfrac{1}{2}.]

Item 5 — Example: Subtracting a Positive Fraction From a Fraction: Unlike Denominators

Example Prompt:
Calculate the value of [MATH: \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{5}{6}.]

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We write [MATH: \dfrac{1}{3}] as [MATH: \dfrac{2}{6}] and then we simply subtract the numerators. This gives
[MATH: \dfrac{2}{6} - \dfrac{5}{6} = \dfrac{2 - 5}{6}.]

Now, we work out [MATH: 2 - 5] using a number line:

[IMG: /graphics/4fcad8d65fffd5f6d03943d5d4beae7a]

So we get
[MATH: \dfrac{2 - 5}{6} = \dfrac{-3}{6} = -\dfrac{3}{6}.]

Finally, we simplify:
[MATH: -\dfrac{3}{6} = -\dfrac{3 \div 3}{6 \div 3} =-\dfrac{1}{2}]

Therefore, we conclude that
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{5}{6} = -\dfrac{1}{2}.]

Item 11 — Example: Subtracting a Positive Fraction From a Fraction: Mixed Numbers

[MATH: 2 \,\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{(2 \times 3) + 2}{3} = \dfrac{8}{3}]

Since both fractions have the same denominators, we can combine them into one fraction, which gives
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{8}{3} = \dfrac{1 - 8}{3}.]

Now, we work out [MATH: 1 - 8] using a number line:

[IMG: /graphics/806362a1e1cbac7eb5b855c621414b4a]

So, we get
[MATH: \dfrac{1 - 8}{3} = \dfrac{-7}{3} = -\dfrac{7}{3}.]

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

[MATH: -\dfrac{7}{3} = -2 \, \dfrac{1}{3}]
